title: SPHEREx 2025-2026 data of 258 dusty field dwarfs and dippers show the 3.1 um ice band only in Gaia20cdd, constant for one year; two dimming events seen by SPHEREx are greyer than interstellar dust
abstract: Question: is the 3.1 um water-ice band of the old dipper Gaia20cdd present in other dusty mature dwarfs and dippers, and what grains do other dimmers have? Method: we read 81x81-pixel boxes from 26,714 SPHEREx Quick Release images (2025 April to 2026 October) with HTTP range requests and made forced PSF photometry of 270 targets (81 TZ25 ZTF main-sequence dippers, 11 campaign dimmers, 178 centroid-clean dwarfs with extreme 12 um excess) and of 10,082 field stars in the same images. We measured the band with the per-exposure ratio method and calibrated it with 5,574 field stars. SPHEREx detectors 1 and 4 see the same sky at the same time, so a dimming event gives 0.9 and 3 um extinction together. Results: a repeat rule (z > 4, depth > 0.10, two visits) selects Gaia20cdd and none of 257 other targets or 5,574 field stars. 95 % upper limits on the fraction with a band of 0.15 or more: 1.7 % of 173 extreme-dust dwarfs and 5.1 % of 57 TZ25 dippers. The mean depth of the extreme-dust dwarfs, after a correction for the shape of their hot-dust continuum, is 0.0025 +- 0.0019 (1/50 of Gaia20cdd). The Gaia20cdd band was 0.31 +- 0.06, 0.36 +- 0.06 and 0.30 +- 0.05 deep in 2025 July, 2025 December and 2026 July (constant; centre 3.096 +- 0.015 um), so its icy screen persisted for one year. SPHEREx saw the TZ25 dipper Gaia DR3 3161408504694560384 in a dip on 2026 April 3: in the same exposures the flux fell to 0.62 +- 0.04 at 0.92 um and at 3.1 um; tau(3.1)/tau(0.92) = 1.02 (95 %: 0.68-1.53; interstellar 0.13), so the occulter is grey (silicate grains of 0.8 um or more, or opaque clumps). The dimmer G2698 faded by 2.4 mag at 0.91 um, 1.0 mag at 2.1 um and 0.8 mag at 3.0 um from 2025 to 2026, a little greyer than interstellar dust (sub-micron grains). Field stars give 2 such events in 3,338. G4466 and G3768 have 850-1000 K excesses; the cold-dust dimmer G2874 has no hot excess and no band. Limitations: preliminary SPHEREx calibration, line-of-sight test only, dippers mostly outside dips, two events with 3-5 exposures per detector, single-size Mie models.
